newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS NAME WAYNE CASHMAN HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS NAME WAYNE CASHMAN HEAD COACH.

text.p: The Philadelphia Flyers Monday named Wayne Cashman as their new head coach, replacing Terry Murray who was fired less than a week after the team was swept in the Stanley Cup finals by the Detroit Red Wings.
This will mark the first NHL head coaching assignment for Cashman, who had been an assistant coach with three different teams.

The 51-year-old Cashman was an assistant for the New York Rangers from 1987-92 and for the Tampa Bay Lightning from 1992-96. He spent one season as an assistant with the San Jose Sharks, but was not tabbed to replace Al Sims, who was fired during the 1996-97 season.
Cashman played 18 seasons for the Boston Bruins, helping the team win Stanley Cups in 1970 and 1972.
Flyers general manager Bobby Clarke fired Murray June 13, even though he led the team to a 45-24-13 record and its first appearance in the Stanley Cup finals in 10 years.
Murray came under heavy criticism for flip-flopping his goalies throughout the playoffs and for publicly accusing his team of choking during the finals with the Red Wings.
Murray, who coached the Flyers for three seasons after coaching the Washington Capitals, reportedly also had a poor relationship his players, especially superstar centre Eric Lindros.
In three seasons with Philadelphia, Murray compiled a 118-64-30 record. His 28 playoff victories place him third on the Flyers' all-time list behind Fred Shero and Mike Keenan.
